===== CLAUDE.md =====

# ONE · platform monorepo

ONE is a SaaS for mass-litigation law firms in Brazil, built in this repository. Many firms share one database from day one (one organization is one firm, isolated by RLS). The first product module covers air-passenger claims against airlines (delays, cancellations, overbooking, baggage) for passengers from all over Brazil. The development plan is `docs/ONE-PLANO-DESENVOLVIMENTO.md` (milestones M0 to M6, approved on 2026-10-08). This repository was copied from the flyee.club platform on 2026-09-30; M0 removed the code that only served that product. The product document is `docs/PRODUCT.md` (rewritten for ONE on 2026-10-22); the other docs, except the plan, still describe flyee.club and are historical.

## Safety

- `apps/web/.env.local` is a blank ONE file. Fill a key only with an ONE development or sandbox credential. The files that pointed at other products are in `C:\AppsProjects\_quarentena-env-one`: never copy them back into the repo.
- Run `db:plan:remote`, `db:migrate:remote`, `db:gate:remote` or `test:db:remote` only while `.env.local` points at an ONE Supabase project (since 2026-10-21, the development one). That project has the baseline, so every change to the database is a new migration file: never edit a migration that a hosted project applied.
- Never commit `.env` or `.env.local`. Commit per milestone; never push without being asked.
- **Finish the work you were given.** Carry each task to its end, and diagnose an ordinary obstacle (an error, a timeout, a locked file, a failing tool) and work through it. Stop only where these rules name a stop: the one step a person must take, a secret, a decision that is the owner's, and what a rule protects. Confirmation before a risky or irreversible action still holds. Close with a recap that stands on its own: what you found and what you did.
- Never store a lawyer's password, 2FA seed or digital certificate (A1, A3 or cloud) anywhere: not in the database, the vault, logs or fixtures, but for the two custodies below. The vault keeps a vendor's API token and nothing else; it refuses the names, and a catalog test refuses such a column. The six digits a WhatsApp number that lives on the platform alone is registered with are typed by the firm, used once and kept nowhere. The owner decided on 2026-10-14 that ONE stores what an automation of its own needs of a lawyer's credentials. Each custody is sealed in the vault as a connection of that lawyer, given only by the lawyer for themself with the second factor, never read by the vault's general read, opened only for a use declared first and kept on record, and ended at once by the lawyer, a partner, who manages the firm, or the lawyer leaving: (1) `0041_cloud_signatures`, the authorization a lawyer gives ONE at the provider of their cloud certificate (a PSC), a signature session's token, never the certificate, its key or its factors, for a certificate of the CPF they declared, at most 7 days, bound to the very files of a package of a lawsuit they sign, what it signed leaving ONE only in their hands, also ended by the PSC or the platform moving its address; (2) `0263_filing_ways`, the lawyer's court login for ONE's own browser (`Vault.sealLawyerCourtLogin`), opened only for a batch they approved (`court_login_open`, 0264), also ended when the court refuses it. A 2FA seed or a certificate's file stays as written above, never through the PSC's optional `pwd_authorize`, which collects the holder's factors: the court's code is asked of the lawyer at each batch.
- `WHATSAPP_SIMULATOR=1` is for a development machine or a preview: production never honours it, a simulated number never reaches the vendor, and a delivery signed by the simulator can only touch simulated numbers. `META_APP_SECRET` is what authenticates every webhook delivery: never commit it.
- `VAULT_KEYS` seals the firms' vendor tokens. Never commit one and never share one between environments. A key that is lost takes every token it sealed with it: the firms reconnect their accounts.
- Fixtures hold invented people only: never a real person's CPF, name or case number. A lawsuit's number in a fixture is of a year to come (2099, with its check digits), so no real lawsuit carries it; a CPF is one every manual uses as an example (123.456.789-09, 529.982.247-25, 111.444.777-35).

## Product decisions the code assumes

- **What needs no person, ONE's own AI does** (the owner, 2026-11-03): a task that asks no decision of a person and that ONE's AI can do from what the firm already has (read a document, fill a record from it, make a model of it, check it against a rule, ask for what is missing) is ONE's work, sparing the firm time, people and cost. A person is asked only what only they know or decide (an answer, a choice of the firm's, a document to send again after a refusal said with why), each firm says how much ONE does alone (`autonomy_decisions`, ONE by default), and what ONE did says that ONE may err. Before suggesting or building a feature, ask first whether ONE can do the task instead of the person, and what it would need to ask; a screen where a person does by hand what ONE could do is the exception, with its reason.
- **ONE's work is never shown as the firm's task** (the owner, 2026-11-03): a checklist, a count, a pending line, an empty state or a message names as the firm's only what a person of the firm does or decides; what ONE does by itself (the case opened at a passenger's yes or from an agency's passenger, the client's link sent, the lawsuits created, the piece written, the package asked for) is said as ONE's work, done, being done, or waited for. A step "Abrir o primeiro caso" on the firm's setup list told a firm that had just finished its setup that the work was manual, against what ONE is sold on: the first case arrives through a module the firm contracted and ONE opens it, so the list ends at what the firm gives ONE (who signs, the team, the channel) and the home says ONE waits for the first case. Opening a case by hand stays, as the exception it is.
- Many firms from day one, with roles inside a firm (sócio, advogado, controladoria, atendimento). A person belongs to one firm at a time (decided by the owner on 2026-10-09; the database enforces it). Passengers never get platform accounts: they reach ONE through links by token.
- A travel agency may be a firm's partner in the passenger module (decided by the owner on 2026-10-29): an account of its own, never a firm's, in partnership with one firm per module at a time. It registers the passengers it covers in an area of its own; the firm reads nothing of them until a passenger says yes to its word about a problem, and the agency nothing of the firm.
- ONE is sold by a technology company with no lawyer partners. It is software for firms: it never acts as a law firm.
- A module of ONE is a package a firm contracts with its subscription (decided by the owner on 2026-10-30): Direito do Passageiro is the first; Direito Previdenciário and Direito Trabalhista are shown as coming soon, and no firm can have them until they are out. The pages of the work read every module or one (the owner, the same day). Since 2026-11-14 there is no menu of the modules nor area of a module (the owner: the access is almost always through Casos, and the area repeated pages the menu has): a module's work is the pages under it (`?modulo=`), the overview of the modules is in the firm's settings (`/settings/modulos`), and the home names them in one line.
- What a partner decides for the firm (who signs, the Valor da Causa Pedido, what ONE decides alone, the words of the clause its agencies register) is decided, in a firm where nobody is a partner, by who manages the firm account.
- **A module is versioned as data** (the owner, 2026-11-11): what a module's cases read (the documents by problem, the version of each of its AI instructions, the platform's piece models) is a version of the module that only the operator publishes and nobody edits once published (a change is a new version); each case keeps the version it was opened under, a new case takes the latest published, and a version withdrawn for a defect sends its cases to the latest published. A new prompt version, document list or platform model reaches a module's cases only through a new published version (a migration or `/admin/modulos`).
- The firm's setup is its core, what every firm needs; what one module needs is that module's own setup, in the module's colour, after the core and before the home, for each module the firm contracted, the others shown disabled; and each person who joins a firm has a setup of their own, the second factor first (the owner, 2026-11-03).
- The module: air-passenger claims. Adults go to the small-claims court (juizado especial cível); a family with a minor goes to the civil court (vara cível) together, in one lawsuit (decided by the owner on 2026-10-14); splitting it (the adults in the small-claims court, the minor in the civil court, linked lawsuits of one case) is a lawyer's recorded choice. An adult above the small-claims ceiling goes to the civil court alone. Each claimant of a lawsuit in the civil court accepts it before the filing. The forum defaults to the passenger's domicile; another forum needs a link to the flight and a recorded reason.
- The notices about a client's own lawsuit go on WhatsApp with no agreement asked; the client stops them on their link, by asking the firm, or with SAIR (decided by the owner on 2026-11-03).
- The Valor da Causa Pedido (what each claimant asks, by kind of problem) is the firm's to give or not: with none, the lawsuit goes with no value defined and the judge defines it (decided by the owner on 2026-10-27).
- Assisted filing: ONE builds the filing package per court system (Projudi, eproc, PJe, e-SAJ); the lawyer files in the court system with their own login. Every certificate type works because signing happens there; where the court's system takes each file already signed (the Projudi of TJGO, a `.p7s`), ONE signs the package's files with the cloud certificate of a lawyer of the lawsuit who authorized it (since 2026-10-15), as the firm lets it.
- **Three ways to file on a court's screen, the lawyer's choice** (the owner, 2026-11-20, accepting the risk in TJGO, TJRJ and TJSP): (1) ONE's own browser with the lawyer's court login (never a 2FA seed or a certificate), the lawyer approving each batch and typing the court's code through ONE when asked; (2) the extension (`apps/web/extension/`) in the lawyer's own session, ONE filling and sending the batch they confirm; (3) by hand, with ONE's package and guide. Asked in the firm's and each lawyer's setup. ONE learns a system's screens at its first filing there, never from a person's map; the lawyer confirms that first one before anything that may send it. A court's written rules are read first (TJGO Res. 59/2016, art. 11; TJRJ Ato 9/2010; TJSP Res. 963/2025, art. 18, I). Portaria CNJ 316/2024, art. 9, lets a court block the lawyer; no way disguises itself or works around a court's restriction (§ 1, V).
- ONE never moves case money and never charges the passenger. It bills only its own subscription (Asaas, BRL). The line of the money (the owner, 2026-11-07, the plan of the controladoria and the finance, decision 1): ONE records, reads, calculates, prepares and warns of a firm's money and its clients'; it never holds, receives, passes on, splits, pays or charges money, not even on a firm's behalf (no account, sub-account, commission, charge, reminder or payment link of a client's), and the code of the firm's books never reaches ONE's own billing (a rule of the lint, `apps/web/eslint.config.ts`).
- WhatsApp through the official Cloud API, with each firm's own number, in coexistence with the phone app; and, as the firm's choice after accepting its risk, through WhatsApp Web by the platform's OpenWA (the owner, 2026-11-11). Either way ONE receives and sends under its database's rules, and the team's panel is Chatwoot (the `whatsapp-support` kit, `packages/atendimento`), which never talks to the vendor.
- **The firm's one WhatsApp, and who goes to a hearing** (the owner, 2026-11-14): the firm connects one WhatsApp, its main number, which ONE uses as the firm's contact; nobody of the team connects theirs, and each person gives their own WhatsApp in their setup, required, by which they are linked to a hearing (its guide, their report). Who goes to a hearing with no account in ONE reports it too: chosen or added where the firm takes notice of the hearing, and kept in the firm's list for the next ones (migration 0251).
- The test chat is offered no longer (the owner, 2026-11-11): a firm tests with its real number once the operator marks it as a test firm (migration 0220), its flights simulated by its tools and its lawsuits answered by the test court.
- The firm's brand on everything a passenger sees. pt-BR only.
- **Decided by the owner on 2026-10-14** (the three decisions the points of 2026-10-13 depended on): what ONE decides alone reaches the lawyer's own acts too (the text of a piece, the decision to file or hold, a deadline), by a parametrization each firm changes, with automation first; a lawyer's certificate, password or second factor is stored when an automation of ONE needs it (the filing in a court's system: the custody and the channel are designed from the notes of 2026-10-14 on the MNI, the courts' systems and the cloud certificates, kept out of the repository); and a family with a minor goes to the civil court together (built, the fifth part of S10).
- **Decided by the owner on 2026-10-15** (on the filing by ONE in a court's own channel, after the research of 2026-10-14): build first what needs no court's authorization (the lawyer's cloud signature through a PSC, the signed file a court takes, the MNI client, each with a stand-in where the vendor or the court stands); never build an automation a court considers fraud, but only where that is certain (a written rule of the court or the CNJ that forbids it); where it is only a forecast, the direct automation (ONE in the court system's own screen, with the lawyer's credentials in custody) may be built. Each court is checked against its written rules before its screen is automated.
- **Decided by the owner on 2026-10-27** (on the travel agency linked to a firm): the passenger's documents an agency attaches come into ONE and ONE uses them, the passenger's agreement given in the agency's contract with them; this replaces "no data passed" of 2026-10-08. Not built yet: how an agency enters ONE (a link of the firm's, an account, an integration with the agency's system) is the owner's to choose, and the legal opinion on soliciting clients (already waited for) answers whether a firm may receive clients so, since the Estatuto da Advocacia (art. 34, IV) forbids taking causes with or without a third party, whatever the client agreed to; the agency's clause has to be a specific consent, highlighted among the others (LGPD, art. 7, § 5, and art. 8, §§ 1 and 4), with a parent's specific consent for a child's data (art. 14, § 1). What an agency attaches is then read as any document (above).
- **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-05** (the audit of the case screen): the case and `/inicio` follow ONE by themselves; a card opens when something comes to ask the firm there and closes once it is done, and its head says where it stands; whether a decision is the judgment is asked only when its words do not say it; the 72-hour notice only warns while the platform is tested, and becomes a block before production (not opening the case, or waiting for a lawyer to release it: to be decided).

## Structure

- `apps/web` — Next.js 15 (App Router) + React 19 + MUI v9 + MUI X's community packages (MIT) + Tailwind 4, deployed on Vercel. See `apps/web/CLAUDE.md`.
  - Auth (`app/auth`, with the firm setup at `auth/complete-profile`), the invitation link (`app/convite/[token]`), the dashboard shell with its gate, the provisional home, the cases, the import of a portfolio and the approval queue (`app/(dashboard)`, `/inicio`, `/casos`, `/casos/importar`, `/casos/[id]`, `/aprovacoes`), the client's page by token (`app/c/[token]`), the public check of a document's code (`app/verificar`), settings (profile, security, team, billing), the operator consoles under `/admin` (firms, leads, billing, AI, audit, backups, announcements, help, blog, support), checkout (`/assinatura`), billing webhooks, the Inngest route, and the provisional public site under `app/[locale]` (home, waitlist, contact, help, blog, legal pages).
- `apps/web/src/modules/<key>` — the product modules' own code (the passenger module: the flights, the flight alerts, the agency's area), reached by the core only through `lib/modules/registry.ts` and `lib/modules/jobs.ts`; their routes are in route groups named after them.
- `packages/design-tokens` — visual identity: `css/blue.css` is the provisional palette (`theme-blue`), `css/common.css` the neutrals and the deep band, `css/marketing.css` the site scale.
- `packages/db` — ONE's baseline: SQL migrations with RLS and explicit grants, the pgTAP suite (two firms in every file), a Drizzle mirror. See its README.
- `packages/auth` — Supabase clients (browser, server, middleware, service role), 2FA step-up, the parallel cookie of support sessions.
- `packages/billing` — ONE's own subscription through Asaas in reais (subscriptions, invoices, coupons, the change of tier and the webhook), the tiers and limits read as data, with a fake and a contract test.
- `packages/email` — Resend + React Email, in Portuguese; no sender throws, all no-op without `RESEND_API_KEY`.
- `packages/jobs` — the Inngest client (id `one`) and its `serve`, which hold no function since the clock moved to ONE's server (`apps/web/clock/`, 2026-11-14); the sweeps and the work after an answer live in `apps/web/src/lib/jobs/`; jobs that write to people follow claim-then-send (its README).
- `packages/audit` — append-only `audit_events`, row versions, versioned consent terms, the sign-in trail.
- `packages/ai` — the model providers behind `ChatProvider` and the executor (`runAiTask`) that runs a task and records it through a store interface; `FakeChatProvider` and `FakeRunStore` for tests and for a machine with no key (its README).
- `packages/connectors` — the vault of the firms' vendor tokens: AES-256-GCM in the backend with `VAULT_KEYS` (never in the database), each seal bound to its firm and account, key rotation, and the refusal of any name that would hold a lawyer's own credential (its README). Its database side is migration `0017_connections`.
- `packages/documents` — the firm's files and the documents ONE issues: what a file is by its bytes and its measure, issuing a version with a public verification code and its mark on every page, the normalization of photos and PDFs for the court systems (its README, with the technical test), the rule that measures how well the photo of a document can be read (`@flyee/documents/quality`), and the attached `.p7s` a court takes, built around a signature made elsewhere (`@flyee/documents/cms`).
- `packages/backup` (the logical backup, never copying the vault: `src/tables.ts`), `packages/fields`, `packages/onboarding`, `packages/content` (`BRAND` and the message catalog `messages/pt-BR.json`).
- **Adapters** — one package per kind of vendor, each with `src/types.ts` (the interface), `src/fake.ts` (in memory, deterministic) and `src/contract.test.ts` (what any implementation must do; the real one joins it with recorded responses): `packages/courts` (the DJEN client with its real implementation over the public API, `@flyee/courts/providers/djen`, the rule of a filing package, `@flyee/courts/filing`, and the sources of the course of a lawsuit, `ProceedingSource`: TJGO's Projudi, Escavador and Judit, with the comparative test, `@flyee/courts/compare`), `packages/signatures` (envelopes of the client's signature), `packages/flights` (flight status and airport weather, with its REDEMET and FlightAware providers, and ANAC's official record of the flights, `@flyee/flights/providers/anac-vra`, with the rule that checks a leg against it, `@flyee/flights/vra` and `@flyee/flights/check`), `packages/identity` (CPF lookup, with its Serpro provider), `packages/calendar` (the firm's calendar of hearings, with its Google provider), `packages/chatwoot` (the firms' panel of attendance: a Chatwoot account per firm with an API inbox ONE writes into, the reading of its signed webhook, migration `0223_chatwoot`, and the team's rooms, inboxes of the team alone, migration `0238_chatwoot_rooms`), `packages/psc` (a lawyer's ICP-Brasil certificate in the cloud: one client for every PSC as DOC-ICP-17.01 specifies it, `@flyee/psc/providers/iti`, and what a certificate says of its holder, `@flyee/psc/certificate`). `packages/signatures` has its ZapSign provider too. Each README says what joins and in which milestone.
- `packages/whatsapp` — the adapter that already has its real implementation: the Cloud API provider for one number of one firm, the reading of the webhooks with the signature check, the steps of Embedded Signup and of coexistence, the submission of a template for approval, the rules a screen needs (the 24-hour window, a template's values and the check of its text) and a simulator that stands where the vendor stands, on both sides (its README says what was verified in the vendor's reference and that none of it ran against Meta yet). Its database side is migration `0019_whatsapp`.
- `packages/rules` — the pure rules of the domain (its README): the CNJ number, flights and airports, the OAB registration, a person's age on a day, the forum, the kind of proceeding, the reading of a METAR, the Tema 1.417 triage, the count of causes per state, the deadline of a procedural act over the court's calendar and the limit to register for oral argument at a session of judgment (`@flyee/rules/sessions`); prescription joins in M4.
- `packages/knowledge` — the pure rules of the firm's library (its README): the reader of what a piece cites, which fails closed, the key and the name of each source as the database writes them, and the measure of how alike two pieces are. Search over the library's texts joins later. `packages/transcribe` stays in commit `ab2e84d`: the transcription became a task of the AI layer (see sprint S6 above).
- `docs/ONE-PLANO-DESENVOLVIMENTO.md` — the plan. `docs/PRODUCT.md` — the product: what ONE is, the owner's decisions, the journey of a case, what ONE decides alone, the vendors, what is open. The other files in `docs/` describe flyee.club and are historical.
- `attachments/` — ONE source material (the deck, the flow maps, the meeting transcript). It stays on the machine and out of the repository (git-ignored, by the owner's decision of 2026-10-09): never commit it, and never copy a real person's data from it into a fixture.

## Engineering rules

1. **Rules are code.** Forum, kind of proceeding, deadlines, prescription, eligibility, the count of cases per state and the Tema 1.417 suspension are pure, versioned, tested functions. AI never decides a rule.
2. **AI suggests and records; the firm says how much ONE decides alone.** Every AI run is stored (task, prompt version, model, effort, input hash, output, cost). Since the owner's decision of 2026-10-14, ONE decides by itself by default and each firm chooses, per decision, to have a person check a share or decide every one (`autonomy_decisions`, `firm_autonomy`); the operator may hold a decision for every firm when its measure falls. A rule (forum, deadline, kind of proceeding) is still code, never the AI's.
3. **Every vendor sits behind an adapter** with a real implementation, a fake and a contract test with recorded responses. No coding task waits for an external key, account or approval. A new adapter follows the seven that exist: sources import their siblings through the package's own exports (`@flyee/courts/types`), tests import with the `.ts` extension, only erasable TypeScript (the contract tests run on `node --experimental-strip-types`), and the package enters `packages/tsconfig.adapters.json` and the root `test:adapters` script.
4. **Configuration is data:** plans, limits, the court-systems table, file limits, forensic calendars, API versions and AI prices live in tables, never in constants.
5. **The firm is on everything:** RLS on every table, explicit grants in every migration, RPCs that receive the firm, the service-role client never handed to an AI tool, and every new pgTAP test runs with two firms.
6. **Jobs are idempotent:** claim-then-send (`for update skip locked`), what is due recomputed from the data on each sweep, never `step.sleepUntil`. The work a person waits on is done right after their answer (`soon`, `apps/web/src/lib/jobs/soon.ts`), never through the job runner; everything else is a sweep listed in `apps/web/src/lib/jobs/registry.ts`, run by the one clock (on ONE's server, `apps/web/clock/`) and, when it serves what people wait on and the clock is silent, while ONE is used. No event is sent to a runner.
7. **Privacy as code:** consent per purpose with frozen text, retention jobs, export and deletion per person, no personal data in logs or error messages, no tracker inside the logged area or the client links.
8. Every mutation records an audit event (`recordAudit` in `apps/web/src/lib/audit.ts`).
9. Visual identity changes ONLY in `packages/design-tokens/css/*.css`; run `npm run tokens:generate` and commit `tokens.generated.ts` with it. The palette is locked to `theme-blue` (provisional) in `apps/web/src/constants.ts`, `apps/web/src/config.ts` and `apps/web/src/style/global.css`. The palette, the logo and the type change only when the owner asks.
10. The logo is the single component `apps/web/src/components/logo/logo.tsx`, reading the provisional ONE art in `apps/web/public/brand/one-*.svg`; every raster is derived by `npm run brand:assets -w @flyee/web`. When the official logo arrives, replace those four SVGs and rerun the script.
11. npm workspaces: install dependencies from the root (`npm install`), never inside an app. The workspace scope stays `@flyee/*` for now.
12. Icons: Phosphor through the tsconfig alias `@/icons/nexture/*` → `src/icons/phosphor/*`.
13. The dark band (footer, deep sections) is `bg-background-deep`. Red is reserved for risk and failure.
14. Copy for people (site, app, e-mails, WhatsApp): pt-BR, plain; no dash (— or –), no exclamation mark, no emoji. Enforced by `apps/web/src/lib/i18n/copy-rules.test.ts`. The operator console is exempt.
15. One language. `LOCALES` (`apps/web/src/constants.ts`) is a list of one and every per-language table is a `Record` over it; a second language is a data change the compiler walks through, never a fork of the code.
16. **No component that needs a paid licence** (the owner's decision of 2026-10-21, as in the MedChina project): MUI X's community packages (MIT) only, and what only a paid tier gives is built in the project's own code. The lint refuses `@mui/x-*-pro`, `@mui/x-*-premium` and `@mui/x-license`, and no licence key exists.

## Shared Claude/Codex harness

- `CLAUDE.md`, `apps/web/CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules/*`, `.claude/skills/*` and `.claude/hooks/*` are the canonical shared sources of the development harness. Do not maintain a second hand-written Codex copy.
- Codex reads the generated `AGENTS.md` mirror and the generated `.agents/skills/*` bridges. `.codex/config.toml` points its lifecycle hooks at the same implementations under `.claude/hooks/`.
- `PostToolUse` runs `scripts/sync-agent-harness.mjs` after canonical harness edits. `npm run harness:check` and `npm run harness:test` also run in the pre-commit hook.
- **The skills of screens are project-agnostic** (the owner, 2026-11-04): `product-screen`, `product-verify` and `marketing-page` hold what any project of this template needs, the fixes of defects met here included (automation before manual work, cards that ask only for what is still owed, counts that match their lists, the latest few on a home, outcomes said where the person acted, nothing typed lost, words that carry the state, the App Router pitfalls, screens judged on fixtures when no sign-in is at hand), written with no product name, so a copy of `.claude/skills/` brings them to another project. ONE's own bindings (its name, its examples, its words) stay in `.claude/rules/app-ux.md`, `.claude/rules/marketing.md` and `apps/web/CLAUDE.md`. When a UI/UX defect is fixed here, its generic lesson goes into the skill and ONE's example into the binding.

## Commands (root)

- `npm run dev` / `build` / `start` / `lint` / `lint:fix` / `prettier` — delegate to `apps/web`.
- `npm run typecheck` — `apps/web` with its pinned TypeScript 5.8, then the adapter packages on their own (`typecheck:adapters`, `packages/tsconfig.adapters.json`). Never run a bare root `npx tsc` on apps/web: it picks the hoisted TS 6.
- `npm run test` — the package tests (`test:ai`, `test:billing`, `test:email`, `test:backup`, `test:connectors`, `test:documents`, `test:rules`, `test:knowledge`, `test:adapters`) plus the web vitest suite. `npm run test:e2e` / `test:a11y` — Playwright against a production build.
- `npm run ci:verify` — everything the `verify` job of CI runs: harness checks, MUI class check, lint, typecheck, tests, the message catalog check, the database reference check, build.
- `npm run check:messages` (`node scripts/prune-messages.mjs --check|--write|--list`) — the message catalog without unused or missing keys.
- `npm run check:db-refs` (`node scripts/check-db-refs.mjs [--list]`) — every table, column, function and argument name the code passes to supabase-js exists in the migrations. Write those names as literals so it can read them.
- `npm run test:db:embedded` — migrations + pgTAP on an embedded PostgreSQL 17, no Docker. `npm run test:db:roundtrip` — the app's own code against that database, one file at a time (the backend's sweeps act across firms), skipped when no database is at hand: a conversation in and out through the simulator (`apps/web/src/lib/whatsapp/roundtrip.db.test.ts`), the firm's panel of attendance written in order and answered there through ONE, and a room of the team made, opened and archived there (`apps/web/src/lib/chatwoot/panel.db.test.ts`), a filing package built from real PDFs, and a test case's filed by ONE in the test court (`apps/web/src/lib/cases/filing.db.test.ts`), a piece written, approved and issued (`apps/web/src/lib/cases/drafts.db.test.ts`), a firm's portfolio brought from a spreadsheet, found in its list and undone (`apps/web/src/lib/import/import.db.test.ts`), the legs of a case checked against ANAC's record and the leg of the problem marked by ONE (`apps/web/src/modules/direito-do-passageiro/flights/checks.db.test.ts`), the course of the lawsuits read from their sources (`apps/web/src/lib/courts/tracking.db.test.ts`), the DJEN read by days with the shadow triage (`apps/web/src/lib/publications/capture.db.test.ts`), a deadline counted over the court's calendar, confirmed and counted again (`apps/web/src/lib/deadlines/deadlines.db.test.ts`), the hearings written to the firm's calendar (`apps/web/src/lib/hearings/hearings.db.test.ts`), the guide of a hearing written for who goes, with ONE's reading (`apps/web/src/lib/hearings/brief.db.test.ts`), the notices to clients sent once each (`apps/web/src/lib/notices/notices.db.test.ts`), a client's photo measured where it arrives, kept, told, sent all the same or taken back (`apps/web/src/lib/cases/document-quality.db.test.ts`), a case carried by ONE from its lawsuits to its filing package (`apps/web/src/lib/cases/advance.db.test.ts`), who has each case, compared with the top of the case (`apps/web/src/lib/cases/standing.db.test.ts`), the whole portfolio of a firm from the database to the file (`apps/web/src/lib/controladoria/portfolio.db.test.ts`), the deadline and the hearing ONE reads from a publication (`apps/web/src/lib/publications/reading.db.test.ts`) and a lawyer's authorization at their PSC kept, used to sign a filing's files and ended (`apps/web/src/lib/psc/signatures.db.test.ts`) and a package's files signed by ONE once the lawyer of the lawsuit authorized it (`apps/web/src/lib/cases/package-signatures.db.test.ts`) and a model of the library prepared from a Word file and a PDF (`apps/web/src/lib/library/imports.db.test.ts`) and a bill in the client's mother's name turned into a declaration of residence signed by gov.br and taken by the filing package (`apps/web/src/lib/cases/residence.db.test.ts`) and a family's free justice asked on the link and declared for the father and the son (`apps/web/src/lib/cases/free-justice.db.test.ts`) and a client's free justice asked for the recurso of the small-claims court, the case already with the court, and the declaration issued by ONE (`apps/web/src/lib/cases/appeal-free-justice.db.test.ts`) and the firm's books kept from an OFX and a CSV statement, a client's money set apart and a receivable settled by ONE (`apps/web/src/lib/finance/books.db.test.ts`) and what a lawsuit came to, read by rule from its movements and its judgment and the case closed by ONE (`apps/web/src/lib/courts/outcome.db.test.ts`); each test, and the setup of each file, has thirty seconds. `npm run db:start` / `db:stop` / `test:db` — the same through local Supabase (needs Docker). The `db:*:remote` scripts are gated: see "Safety".
- `npm run db:schema:pull` — regenerate the Drizzle mirror from the migrations.
- `npm run tokens:generate` — regenerate the TS token mirror. `npm run brand:assets -w @flyee/web` — regenerate the brand rasters.
- `node scripts/djen-systems.mjs [--day YYYY-MM-DD] [--courts TJGO,TJSP] [--json out.json]` — samples the public DJEN API and counts, per court, the system each communication links to (only hosts and counts). It shows where cases in course live; new cases may already go to another system, so confirm with the court's acts.
- CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs two jobs on every pull request and every push to `main` (beside the deploy, which does not wait for it), with no secrets and no deploy: `verify` (the steps of `ci:verify`) and `database` (`test:db:embedded`, then `test:db:roundtrip`).

## Platform decisions

- Deploy: Vercel, only through GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`) with the Vercel CLI and a token, as in MedChina (since 2026-10-21): a push to `main` deploys production, a pull request a preview, and a manual run production unless preview is chosen. A production deploy then ships the platform's one clock, bundled from the same commit, to ONE's server (the shared VPS, `one@187.53.106.93`, `/opt/atendimento/one/relogio`; since 2026-11-14, by the owner's yes, when the clock's beats on Vercel were most of what the Hobby plan allows): `apps/web/clock/` (`main.ts`, `build.mjs`, `compose.yml`, and `receber.sh`, the one command the deploy key `ONE_VPS_CLOCK_KEY` may run there), with its keys in `/opt/atendimento/one/segredos/relogio.env`; each beat marks `clock_beat` in `platform_settings`, and the app runs its own rounds while ONE is used only when that mark is older than fifteen minutes. The deploy still syncs Inngest, which holds no function of ONE any more. The Vercel project is `one-platform` of the team ONE (the Vercel account `onedeveloperapp`), never connected to GitHub on the Vercel side, with its root at `apps/web`, the files outside it included, Node 22 and its functions in São Paulo (`gru1`); its production address is `one-platform-two.vercel.app`, public and indexable (each deployment's own address sits behind Vercel's login). The first deploy, of `f4e0c2a`, went up on 2026-10-21 with no database: the public site, served from `gru1`. The owner then set on Production the Supabase keys (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`), `VAULT_KEYS` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; `WHATSAPP_SIMULATOR`, `CALENDAR_FAKE` and `PSC_FAKE` are set there too, and production honours none of them (they act on a preview). The repository's secrets are `VERCEL_TOKEN`, `VERCEL_ORG_ID` and `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID`. Every commit is authored as `onedeveloperapp <onedeveloper.app@gmail.com>`, the owner of the Vercel account, set in this repository's own git config (MedChina's commits are `flayeelab`'s the same way): on the Hobby plan Vercel builds only a commit whose author is the team's owner, and blocks any other (`TEAM_ACCESS_REQUIRED`) while the workflow waits for it. On this machine the Vercel CLI's own login is another account's: the ONE account is used as `vercel -Q C:\Users\tribo\.vercel-one <command>`, and `.vercel/project.json` (git-ignored) links the repository to the project. Database, auth and storage: Supabase (Postgres + RLS). ORM: Drizzle. Email: Resend. Jobs: one clock on ONE's server (every five minutes, 2026-11-14; at Inngest from 2026-11-04 to then), and the work a person waits on right after their answer (2026-11-04). The screens that follow the database (`useLiveRead`) ask their pulse from the browser straight to Supabase, never through the app's host. Billing of the ONE subscription: Asaas (BRL).
- Without a database the app still builds and serves the public site: forms answer that they are unavailable, legal pages say they could not load, and the logged area redirects to sign-in. That is what a preview shows until an ONE Supabase project exists.
- Locale: pt-BR only.
- Do not introduce Cloudflare-specific services (Workers, D1, R2, Workers AI).

This repo stays **private**.

===== apps/web/CLAUDE.md =====

# ONE web (apps/web)

Next.js 15 (App Router) + React 19, the only app of ONE: the firm's area, the operator consoles, checkout, auth and the public site. See the root `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/ONE-PLANO-DESENVOLVIMENTO.md`.

**`apps/web/ARCHITECTURE.md` is the map of how the app works, area by area, with its files, tables, migrations and sweeps.** Read the section of the area before changing it (the stack in full; the gate, the menu and entitlements; the firm, its team and sign-up; the home and the modules; the setups; the owner's rules of screens; cases and the portfolio import; conversations; filing; publications; deadlines; hearings; the library; approvals; the controladoria; the books, the numbers and ONE's work; people and their data; screens, entry by entry; settings and connections; the client's link and verification; the agency module; usage events; the public site; billing and checkout; the team console; AI runs and spend; the vault and files; WhatsApp; account plumbing; messages and background work; the state of 2026-10-09), and update that section in the same change when a mechanism is added or moved. This file keeps the rules every change in `apps/web` obeys, beside the root `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/rules/*`.

## Stack and conventions

- **UI**: before building a component, look for a MUI v9 or MUI X community (or Lab) equivalent. Import the one icon you render, through `@/icons/nexture/*`; `src/icons/icon-registry.tsx` ships the whole set and is for the menu only.
- **Styling**: MUI theme driven by CSS variables (`hsl(var(--token))`) from `@flyee/design-tokens`. Component overrides live in `src/style/**/*.css` inside CSS layers (`theme, base, mui, components, utilities`). Tailwind 4 for layout utilities, merged with `tailwind-merge`. Run `npm run check:mui-classes` after touching `src/style/**`.
- **Themes**: the palette and the mode are classes on `<html>` that the root layout renders on the server, and a script in `<head>` corrects the mode before the first paint. Never leave them to a client effect: until it ran, the page had no palette.
- **Fonts and shapes**: radius, shadows and the card's hairline are tokens of `packages/design-tokens/css/common.css`; cards and papers are `rounded-xl`; Tailwind's important modifier takes no space (`shadow-sm!`, checked by `check:mui-classes`). Change the faces only when the owner asks.
- **Forms**: Formik + Yup. Semantic data (phone, CPF/CNPJ, CEP, money) uses `components/product/fields/*`, never a raw `TextField`; persist digits, never masks.
- **i18n**: every user-facing string goes through next-intl and the one catalog, `packages/content/messages/pt-BR.json`. `node scripts/prune-messages.mjs --check` fails on unused and missing keys; `src/lib/i18n/messages.test.ts` refuses a blank text.
- **Language of a request**: Portuguese. A public page keeps the locale in its internal URL (`app/[locale]/`); everything else renders in the default locale. No language cookie, no detection, no switch.
- **Path alias and brand**: `@/*` → `./src/*`. Identity comes from `@flyee/content` through `src/brand.ts`; the logo component never redraws its SVGs.
- **Remote data**: `lib/remote-state.ts` (`RemoteState<T>`: idle, loading, success, empty, error). An error is never rendered as empty.

## Logged area (product layer)

- **Screen shape**: `page.tsx` is a server component that reads with the person's session (`lib/member/context.ts`, `getMemberContext()`, cached per request: the session client, the firm with the person's role and function, `isSuperadmin`, currency and `org_entitlements`) and hands a `state` (`ready` | `error` | `unavailable`) to a client view that takes plain props. An error is never rendered as an empty state, and every write goes to the database function that owns the rule.
- **The gate and the menu are guidance, not the fence**: row-level security and `require_aal2()` are. Both are pure and unit-tested (`lib/firm/gate-rules.ts`, `lib/firm/menu.ts`) and get who is looking from the server layout, so the first paint is right. The middleware passes the path in `x-one-path` and stays query-free.
- **Entitlements**: `org_entitlements(org)` is the single answer to what a firm may use. Screens branch on it, never on plan names; limits are data on the plan rows.
- **The firm and its team**: every change is a server action calling the database function that takes the firm; no rule is decided in TypeScript. Colleagues are read through `firm_team()`, never `profiles`; a query on `memberships` always filters by `user_id`. `handle_new_user` creates the profile and nothing else; a campaign attaches to the firm when it is founded, never at sign-up.
- **Modules**: a page under `?modulo=<key>` keeps `modulo` in every link it builds. What only a module has is offered under that module and in its area, never on a page of every module. The core opens a module's component through the registry (`next/dynamic`), never by name; a new module brings its setup in its own folder and touches nothing of the core's; a module not contracted is never set up.
- **The setup checklist**: a step is done when the thing exists in the database (`firm_setup_facts(org)`), never because somebody clicked.
- **The owner's rules of screens** (in full, with ONE's examples, in `.claude/rules/app-ux.md`): the setup never leads away from itself; whatever a later step needs is a step before it, the second factor first; ONE does the work and a person answers only what only they know or decide; a registration starts from documents, and typing is the contingency; a card asks only for what is still owed and says where each thing stands.
- **Searches and court texts**: a search (a name, a CPF, a number) goes in the request, never in the address. A court's text is rendered as plain text, never as markup. Never `select("*")` on `publications`: a list reads `PUBLICATION_LIST_COLUMNS`, and the AI's shadow answer is not a member's to read.
- **Pages by token** (`/convite/[token]`, `/c/[token]`, `/verificar`): no tracker, no referrer. A client's link shows the firm's name only, is never indexed, and writes only through its `client_link_*` functions.
- **Usage events** are events, never content (vocabulary and properties in migration 0007). In the browser, end the PostgREST builder with `.then()`: a bare `void supabase.rpc(...)` never sends the request.
- **No tracker runs inside the logged area**: it shows client names and case numbers. The Pixel and GA4 exist on the public site only.
- Reusable blocks live in `components/product/*` and are listed in `components/product/catalog.json` (injected by the `product-screen-guard` hook). Every zero-data view uses `EmptyState`.

## Public site (marketing layer)

- The layer's own rules are in `.claude/rules/marketing.md` (the primitives, SEO and the sitemap, Markdown content, motion, the declared site events, no loading boundary above a public page; each signed-in area keeps its own boundary in its layout). Display type is `font-display text-display-{2xl,xl,lg,md}`.
- A new public page is declared in `src/i18n/routing.ts`, which also makes it public to the middleware.
- **The loader overlay is for the signed-in areas only** (`isPublicPageRequest()`). What a public page decides in the browser above the fold is decided before the first paint, from `<head>`, never after hydration.
- **Performance of the public site**: what a public page pays on a phone is the shared shell (MUI and its styling engine hydrate on every page, and one stylesheet carries the overrides of every dashboard component). Do not add to that cost: no scripted animation, no client component where a server one does, one icon import per icon.
- Legal pages render the version in force of `consent_terms`, so the page shows exactly the text people accept; the catalog holds no second copy of the terms.
- Every primary CTA follows the launch stage (`lib/launch.ts`): `/espera` in `waitlist`, sign-up in `open`.
- A public form never reveals whether an address was already listed. A token in an e-mail link (`/espera/confirmar`, the unsubscribe link) moves into an httpOnly cookie and the page loads at the clean address; confirming takes a button press, because mail scanners open every link.
- **Tracking**: the Meta Pixel and GA4 run on the public site only, server-rendered behind one opt-out cookie and one notice (`lib/analytics.ts`); conversions go server-side (`lib/meta-capi.ts`, `lib/ga4-mp.ts`); the snippets are written once, in `lib/tracker-snippets.ts`.

## Billing

- The ladder inherited from the previous product (one-time access, USD through Stripe, `@flyee/billing/entitlements`) is not extended; ONE's own subscription replaces it. Provider webhooks are idempotent (`claim_billing_webhook_event`); `billing_past_due_grace_ends()` is the one answer every gate shares; a comped plan goes only through `set_org_plan`; prices on screen go through `formatPrice`, never struck through.
- ONE never moves case money: billing is the firm's own subscription and nothing else.

## Platform admin and account

- **Console shape**: a page reads through `lib/admin/*` inside `loadConsole()` (a failed read is never an empty list) and hands plain props to a client view; a write is a server action that calls `requireSuperadmin()` again, records an audit event and uses the database function that owns the rule wherever one exists. Its copy is hardcoded pt-BR, outside i18n (code comments stay in English); formatting goes through `lib/admin/format.ts`, and a database value becomes a word through `lib/admin/labels.ts`, never shown raw.
- The dossier of a firm (`/admin/escritorios`) shows its ACCOUNT, never what the firm keeps in the product. The Admin menu group renders only for the platform operator.
- **The superadmin flag** changes only through `set_user_superadmin(user, value, note)`: a trigger on `profiles` fences it by who is asking, and self-change is refused.
- **Support impersonation**: the write fence is in the database (`is_impersonated()`); a visit runs on a parallel session cookie; ending it uses `signOut({ scope: "local" })`, never the global default; starting it needs the operator's own session at AAL2 and a reason.
- **Account deletion** keeps its fixed order: re-read the preview, cancel any live provider subscription (a failure deletes nothing), run the RPC in one transaction, then remove storage through `admin_orphaned_account_storage`.
- **AI runs** go through `runFirmTask(request)` of `lib/ai/executor.ts`, never straight to a provider from a page, a route or a job: that call would be neither recorded, priced nor approved. `AI_FAKE_PROVIDER=1` is the fake on a machine with no key. `ai_spend` is written only inside `finish_ai_run`; prices are configuration (`platform_settings`, `ai_prices`).
- **The vault**: `getVault()` is the one way to a firm's vendor token, for jobs and webhooks only, opened once per batch of work with the firm and a purpose (every open is audited). A page never opens a token; a secret never goes into `connections.metadata`.
- **Files**: `startUpload`, `finishUpload` and `downloadUrl` (`lib/files/*`) are the only way to the `firm-files` bucket; the bytes never pass through a route of the app.
- **Issued documents** (`lib/documents/*`): `issueFirmDocument(input, render)` is the one way a document is issued; the renderer prints the verification mark with `stampVerification`. `lib/documents/verification.ts` holds the pure rules of the public page.
- **WhatsApp**: every delivery enters by `handleDelivery(rawBody, signature)` (`lib/whatsapp/inbox.ts`), the webhook and the simulator alike; a person's message goes out in two halves, `sendMessage` then `deliverOutbox`; `providerFor` is the one way to a number's provider. Never call the vendor, or write a `wa_*` table, in another way. Before the backend's half acts for a connection it asks the session the two questions of `lib/whatsapp/session.ts` (not a support visit, the second factor confirmed). The vendor's SDK loads only on `/settings/connections`, after the person asks to connect.
- Notification rows are created server-side with `lib/notifications.ts`.

## Messages: bell, e-mail and scheduled jobs

- **Every message to a person** comes from one copy object per channel: bell texts in `lib/messages/bell-copy.ts` (written by `notifyLocalized`), e-mail copy in `packages/email/src/copy/pt-BR.ts`. Never write a sentence for a person at a call site.
- **A plan is called by `plans.name`**, never by a word in the copy. A date and an amount arrive already formatted for the reader (`lib/messages/format.ts`: the reader's time zone, `America/Sao_Paulo` when unknown).
- **Claim, then send** (root rule 6): where there is no row to mark, the bell's unique `source_key` is the fence and the e-mail goes only with a new bell row. A message may be lost to a failed send, never sent twice; a batch the provider refuses is given back (`settle_newsletter_batch`).
- **Without `RESEND_API_KEY` or Inngest nothing breaks**: senders return `{ sent: false }` with no error, the bell still rings, a job does not claim what exists only as e-mail, and what an action starts runs after its answer.
- **What a reader can stop** (the news, the list) carries `unsubscribeUrl(...)` in the body and as `List-Unsubscribe`; `/api/public/email/unsubscribe` acts on POST only. Receipts and account notices ignore the preference.
- **Sweeps** (`Sweep` of `lib/jobs/schedule.ts`) are declared beside their code and listed in `lib/jobs/registry.ts`: one missing there never runs. A sweep claims each work in the database; one that must never run from two servers at once runs from the clock only; its answer holds counts only.
- **Billing notices** go through `lib/billing-notices.ts` and never throw: by the time one runs the database is already right, and a webhook that failed on a bell would be replayed by the provider and reconcile the whole event again.
- **Auth e-mails** are Supabase's templates (`supabase/templates/*.html`), not the app's.

## Auth

- Supabase through `@flyee/auth` (`client`/`server`/`middleware`/`service`). `src/middleware.ts` refreshes the session and protects everything except the public pages (`matchPublicPath`, from `src/i18n/routing.ts`) and `PUBLIC_PREFIXES`. Without `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`/`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` the middleware no-ops and the auth screens show a configuration hint.
- 2FA (TOTP): enrolled at `/settings/security`; the middleware forces the AAL2 step-up at `/auth/two-factor`. M1 makes it mandatory by role.
- Internal redirects go through `lib/safe-next.ts` (`sanitizeInternalNext`), never a raw `next` parameter.

## Commands (run from the monorepo root)

- `npm run dev` — dev server. `npm run build` — production build. `npm run typecheck` — TypeScript 5.8 pinned to this app.
- `npm run test:web` — vitest. `npm run test:e2e` / `npm run test:a11y` — Playwright against a production build (`e2e/baseline.spec.ts`).
- `npm run lint:fix` / `npm run prettier` — lint and formatting.

## Watch out

- `src/style/global.css` imports tokens from `@flyee/design-tokens/css/*`; never recreate tokens locally.
- Deploys go ONLY through GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, manual dispatch); the Vercel Git integration stays disconnected.
- Server-only secrets (`DATABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, provider keys) never reach client components.
- `apps/web/.env.local` is a blank ONE file: fill a key only with an ONE development or sandbox credential (root `CLAUDE.md`, "Safety").
- After deleting a route, remove `apps/web/.next/types` before `npm run typecheck`: the generated route types of the last build still name it.

===== .claude/rules/app-ux.md =====

---
paths: ["apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/**", "apps/web/src/components/product/**"]
---

# Product (authenticated app) UX

- The `product-screen` skill is MANDATORY for any create/edit here — a `PreToolUse` hook (`.claude/hooks/product-screen-guard.mjs`) loads it automatically; you never wait to be asked.
- **Goal, not table**: design from the user's job and what success looks like. Never default to a CRUD table of rows — that shape is allowed only when the job really is scan/compare/manage many rows.
- **Never a blank screen**: every zero-data view uses `EmptyState` (icon + why + the ONE next action). A brand-new user must find a path to value (the aha moment).
- **Less text on the screens, and no empty space** (the owner, 2026-11-09): a page, a card or a section opens on its title, and what it is for sits behind the "i" beside it (`description` of `PageHeader`, `CardTitle`, `CollapsibleCard` and `SectionTitle`; 200 characters at most, kept by `lib/i18n/hint-budget.test.ts`). `detail` keeps in sight only state or data (the kind of a case, a conversation's number, how many a list shows) and what must be read before acting (leaving the firm, what each decision of `/settings/autonomia` does, what a lawyer authorizes with the cloud signature, the release of a real passenger's alerts, and the instructions on the client's and the passenger's own pages). A row or a column that opens a list shows a chevron, never a sentence saying so; a definition that repeats its title goes; a tile is its icon and its name. A section with nothing in it takes a drawing of `@/icons/illustrations` (`EmptyState` `illustration`): the court with no lawsuit, the board with no case going, the goals with none, a module with no case, and every list with nothing in it (the cases, the conversations, the publications, the deadlines, the agenda, the filing queue, the library, the approvals, the operator's consoles); a state of permission or of a failed read keeps its icon. The owner found the controladoria, a module's area and the library tiring to read: 136 blocks of text under titles, about 2,800 words. The case screen had the same, card by card (2026-11-10): each card with nothing in it takes its drawing beside its words (the dossier's, in the narrow column, above them), a section inside a card says what it is behind the "i" of its sub-heading (`SectionTitle` `variant="subtitle2"` `as="h3"`: the suspension of the Tema 1.417, the acceptance of the civil court, the audios of the case, the preview of a piece), the way out of ONE's automation (a petition written outside, the reason a family goes together) sits behind an `InfoHint` beside its state line, and a state line drops the sentence that repeats the button beside it.
- **Onboarding never diverts attention**: a setup or onboarding screen (`/configurar`, the setup on the home, any `SetupWizard`) carries nothing that leads away from finishing it: no link to another screen, no "see more", no list of things to explore. Each step does its work in place (dialogs, inline forms, the second factor in the step); what is information for later lives on the home or its own page. A line of modules with "Ver módulos" on the first step of `/configurar` took the owner out of a setup half done (2026-10-30).
- **Prerequisites come first**: in a setup or any multi-step flow, whatever a later step cannot be done without (the second factor, a role, a connection, a fact the database checks) is its own step before the first step that needs it, and the flow does not advance past it until it is met. Never let a person reach a step and find it locked by something an earlier step could have settled. The second factor is the first step of `/configurar` for this reason (2026-11-03): it was asked inside six steps, and blocked the owner at the first.
- **ONE does the work, a person answers** (the owner, 2026-11-03): before a screen has a person do a task by hand, ask whether ONE's AI can do it from what the firm already has (read a document, fill a record from it, make a model of it, check it against a rule, ask for what is missing), and build that instead. The screen shows what ONE did and that ONE may err, and asks only what only the person knows or decides; a document ONE cannot use is refused with why and the way to send another. How much ONE does alone is each firm's (`autonomy_decisions`, ONE by default). The setup's step of the papers had no way to send the firm's own power of attorney: the firm sends the document it already uses, and ONE makes the model (migration 0079). The model keeps the firm's words (0093): only what changes per case becomes a mark, each field of the firm's form its own (`[[NOME]]`, `[[CPF]]`, `[[ENDERECO]]`), and the firm's society and lawyers stay as written once it says they are its own; the case says when a lawyer who signs is not among them.
- **ONE's work is never the person's task** (the owner, 2026-11-03): a checklist, a count, a pending line, an empty state or a message names as the person's only what a person does or decides. What ONE does by itself (opens a case from a module, sends a link, creates the lawsuits, writes a piece) is said as ONE's work, done, being done or waited for ("O ONE espera o primeiro caso"), never as a step the person owes, and a manual way to do it is offered as the exception it is, never as the primary action. "Abrir o primeiro caso" on the firm's setup list made a firm that had just finished its setup feel the work was manual, the opposite of what ONE is sold on.
- **A registration starts from documents** (the owner, 2026-11-03): where the record is already written on a document the person has (an identity, a proof of address, a ticket, a booking's screenshot, a photo of a printed page), the form opens on sending it; ONE reads it, fills the fields and marks each as read, and the person confirms or corrects what ONE read, being asked by hand only what no document gives. Typing every field is the contingency, offered as "Preencher à mão", never the first screen. The agency's new passenger was a form of typed fields while ONE already read the identity, the proof of address and the ticket on the passenger's page; it now starts from them (migration 0083). A document sent for one job fills every record it carries: the power of attorney and the contract the firm sends for its models fill "Dados do escritório" (the address, the e-mail, the society's registration, the CNPJ, the lawyers) where it has nothing, marked "Lido pelo ONE" until a person confirms (0271); the setup had asked by hand for the address both papers wrote.
- **A card asks only for what is still owed** (the owner, 2026-11-03): a request already fulfilled (a document that arrived and serves, a link already sent, an answer given) leaves the card's main area. The card says it as done (`StateLine` `done`, a green check; when nothing is left in the card, one line on its tint that says so: "Não precisa enviar de novo") and keeps doing it again one click away, in `QuickActions`. What is still owed, or arrived and does not serve, is its own line in the attention colour with its one button beside it. The passenger's link showed "Enviar identidade" to a passenger whose agency had already sent it.
- **Where things stand is said in icon and colour**: every card a person works through leads with the icon of what it is (`CardTitle`, its family's tint) and says where it stands in a `StatusChip`; each thing listed in it says its state in a `StateLine`: done in green with a check, under way in amber with a clock, to look at or act on in accent-3 with an exclamation, a failure in red (kept for failures), information in grey. The words always say the state too, never the colour alone.
- **An act the person must understand is confirmed in front of them**: what binds them or what others will act on (an agreement given or taken back, a decision) is confirmed in an `OutcomeDialog`: the state in a large icon, the title in their words ("Acordo registrado"), each consequence on its own line with its icon, one button ("Entendi"). A line of `Alert` at the top of the page is read past: the passenger who agreed on their link could not tell what they had agreed to start.
- The record of each screen (what it shows, its files and migrations, and what the owner found behind it) is in `apps/web/ARCHITECTURE.md`, under its area. Read it before changing a screen, and write the new entry there in the same change; the rules those entries gave are below.
- **The case says what happens now, and one action runs at a time.** The top of `/casos/[id]` says what ONE is doing, what holds the case and whose turn each thing is; every wait's owner comes from one table (`WAIT_PLACE` of `lib/cases/advance.ts`). The case and `/inicio` follow the database by themselves (`useLiveRead`). A write a card starts goes through `useCaseAction(section).run`: the other controls wait disabled with why, reading stays free, the lock lifts once the case is read again, and what came of it is said in that card. When it moved the case's trail, the screen goes to "Andamento do caso", which marks itself (`showTrail`), and what came of it stays one "Ver" away. A card's list that piles up is `ItemRows`: what asks first, then ONE's work, then what is settled, each line's standing a pure rule. While ONE works on a record its screen waits under `AtWorkNotice`, for ONE's own work only.
- **One rule per fact.** Who has a case is `case_standing` on every screen, and a count never comes from another rule. `/casos` is the only page that lists the cases, and a count opens a list of the size it says. Two views of one menu never share a name. "Com o escritório" is of the trip that became a case, never of the passenger (`passengerStanding`).
- **Each setting has one home** (the owner, 2026-11-11). "Sua conta" is the person's (Perfil, Segurança, Atuação profissional); "Escritório" is the firm's (Dados do escritório, Equipe, Regras dos casos, O que o ONE decide, Mensagens ao cliente, Conexões, Plano e pagamentos, Apagar dados de teste); each contracted module has its group (`firmSettings` of its definition). "O que o ONE decide" holds only ONE's decisions, by the stage of the case; the agenda, `/publicacoes` and the setups say how a setting is and lead to its home or use its component.
- **ONE acts, and the person is told.** An automation that acts on what it classified is applied at once and asks the person's awareness after it ("Estou ciente"), with the way to correct it. What ONE's work needs of a person is asked when the work starts. A wait on the client always has a way forward for a partner or a lawyer. A state that may have changed is never said as unchanged. An alarm counts only what a person can put right. Each decision is made where it belongs, on its case or in its conversation, and `/aprovacoes` never holds the text of a piece.
- **What a piece asks.** The client is interviewed one question at a time. A piece writes `[COMPLETAR]` only for a fact its claim cannot stand without, and ONE asks the client the rest. A name ONE read is said corrected only when its words changed.
- **The firm's hard lines.** A filing that may have reached the court is never sent again until a lawyer says the court's system lacks it. ONE never charges a client, never tells a client of a judgment by itself, and nothing on a screen says ONE pays. A fact ONE read is corrected with its reason, never deleted. What ONE did is counted for the firm, never per person. The fees and the books show only to who reads the books; a client's money is never revenue; a line that may repeat another is said, never dropped; a number never averages fewer than five lawsuits.
- **People's data.** A CPF in a list shows only its middle. Refusing marketing never stops the notices of a lawsuit, and a segment never holds a minor nor who refused marketing. Exporting or erasing a person's data, and taking the whole portfolio, are for who decides for the firm, with the second factor; "Levar a carteira inteira" is a button in plain sight, never in a menu. What leaves ONE (an e-mail, a calendar link) names the act and the case's number, never a typed title.
- **Every registration is managed the same way.** The list with `ListBar` and its "Novo" (none on a list of what ONE makes; making one by hand stays in "Mais ações"); creating and editing in `SidePanel`, the document first where there is one; what another record uses is archived with its reason, and only what nothing uses is deleted, in a `ConfirmActionDialog`; every change audited, and the finance's registrations ask the second factor. "Adicionar" at the top offers what this person may add, never on a setup nor to a partner's people.
- **Lists, numbers and exports.** A list's view and order live in the address, so a tile opens the view it counts; a search goes in the request. A page of numbers only shows: each number opens `/casos` with the page's cut, it says whether it counts test cases, and what ONE does not count yet is said so, never drawn as zero. A test case says "Teste" wherever it is listed. An export saves nothing of a list it could not read whole and says on its first page what it is. A board ONE moves never offers to drag a card. A package something holds is "Com impedimento", never "Pronto para protocolar".
- **The home lays out by what it holds** (the owner, 2026-11-12): under the greeting, what holds a case in the wide column, what to follow (`CountList`) and ONE's line of the month in the side one, a column with nothing in it not drawn and the other then across; the portfolio's card across below. A line, a list of one and a tile of one each across `/inicio` left most of it empty.
- **Cards in a row line up** (the owner, 2026-11-12): the controladoria's board has its columns after the plans of a pricing page, sharing their rows, each part of the way named over its columns in one colour, an empty column saying "Nenhum caso" in its shape; "Com quem está" and "Tribunal" are two cards of one height with the same head. The court's numbers had been a heading over seven cards beside a card.
- **Who owes what, where, with what** (the owner, 2026-11-12, on the people's card of the case): a card's head says one state (`ask` of `CollapsibleCard` with the screen's state, never a chip beside it); what the client owes says who answers it and since when, from their link (`client-asked.tsx`), with "Preencher pelo cliente" or "Enviar pelo cliente" as the exception; a fix that lives on another card leads there (`#case-people`); "Confira" comes with the document, both values or the source in front; facts under their names (`FactGrid`); "Depende da plataforma" for what the platform owes, nothing of the environment. The leg of the trip's problem is ONE's to mark (0228), and the card asks a person only when the record cannot tell.
- **Pessoas laid out by what filters what** (the owner, 2026-11-12): the funnel's cards right over the list they filter, each with its share in a ring (`NumberCard` `ratio`); the numbers of who the firm serves after the list, as `TallyTile`s four across; a trend drawn only where a series exists.
- **A record inside a card reads in one order** (the owner, 2026-11-13, on a lawsuit of "Processos"): head (name, one state, its edit and "⋯"), facts filling their rows with ONE's reasons behind each fact's "i" (`FactGrid` `hint`), what is owed as one line each with its answers beside it, then its foot; never a box with its own chip inside the record.
- **The library says what waits and what ONE writes with** (the owner, 2026-11-13): "Esperam você" first (what ONE asks, a model ready to check, a refusal, a citation with no source, one button each), then "Com que modelo o ONE escreve" (a tile per use: the petition of each kind of lawsuit with its models by problem, each paper and declaration, the pieces of the process), then the list; "Novo modelo" opens on the upload, what ONE read marked "Lido pelo ONE", "Modelo padrão" ticked and said when the firm has none of its own for that use; ONE compares the firm's data in a document with its record and never asks what matches (0244).
- **The client's page follows what the client does** (the owner, 2026-11-13): one rule (`clientStanding`) gives the head's count, the numbered steps in the order of the case and "Já feito"; each section in one frame (`ClientSection`), its own card or its content inside a step; what the firm asks of a hearing beside the hearing; the lawsuit in one card; nothing says "ONE" to the client.
- **The forecast is the case's, at a glance, and never a promise** (the owner, 2026-11-14): one rule (`market_forecast_of`) on every screen; the case shows it open under its top (chance as a ring, the value as a range, how it ends, each level beside it), the next hearing what the airline does there and where an offer falls, `/numeros` the sum and how it came out; the base and the sample always said, "pode errar" behind the "i"; never on the client's page, never to choose a judge.
- **A card's actions in one place each** (the owner, 2026-11-12, from "Incluir trechos" beside "+ Incluir pessoa"): adding to a card's list is `add` of `CollapsibleCard` ("+ Incluir ..." at the foot), the list elsewhere is `more` ("Ver ... ›" at the foot), the top keeps only what acts on the whole record; an item's edit at its head, its removal in its "⋯"; adding says "Incluir".
- **Shape.** Every route of the logged area has a `loading.tsx` drawing `PageSkeleton` in its form, and a new page gets its own. A state on a menu item floats over it (`CornerTag` `edge`), and a submenu closes once a page is reached. There is no menu of the modules (the owner, 2026-11-14): a module's work is the pages under it, its overview is in the firm's settings, and the home names the modules in one line.
- **Core and module setups are apart** (the owner, 2026-11-03): a setup asks what every firm needs in the core (`/configurar`) and what one module needs in that module's own setup, in the module's colour, after the core and before the home, only for the modules the firm contracted; the others are shown disabled, as what the firm could add. Never put a module's parameter in the core's setup, nor ask a firm to set up a module it does not have.
- **Everybody who joins has a setup of their own**: a firm's member, an agency's colleague; the second factor first, then what their function needs (a lawyer's registration at the bar), never a home with nothing said.
- Long setups use `SetupWizard` (progressive disclosure); steps to first result use `OnboardingChecklist` + `@flyee/onboarding` (state only; step definitions live in the project's code).
- **Engagement**: completion drive (`ActivationProgress`) and competence feedback only. Never ship points, badges, leaderboards or streaks — documented failures, and streaks carry regulatory risk.
- MUI v9 + theme tokens only, next-intl for every string, inline form errors near the field, skeletons that reserve space.
- **Semantic fields**: phone, CPF/CNPJ, CEP and money never go in a raw `TextField` — use `components/product/fields/*` (mask + check-digit validation + CEP auto-fill via `@flyee/fields`); persist `onlyDigits()`, never the masked string.

===== .claude/rules/design-tokens.md =====

---
paths: ["packages/design-tokens/**", "apps/web/src/style/**"]
---

# Design tokens

- `packages/design-tokens/css/*.css` is the source of truth for visual identity. `src/tokens.generated.ts` is GENERATED — never edit it manually.
- After any change in `css/*.css`, run `npm run tokens:generate` at the root and include the generated file in the same commit.
- Color values are bare HSL triplets (`191 100% 46%`), consumed via `hsl(var(--token))` in CSS. Keep this format; do not introduce hex/rgb.
- Every color token must exist in light/dark pairs (`:root`/`.dark` in common, `.theme-x`/`.theme-x.dark` in theme files).

===== .claude/rules/icons.md =====

---
paths: ["apps/web/src/icons/**", "apps/web/src/app/**"]
---

# Icon contract

- Pages import icons only as `@/icons/nexture/ni-*` (the alias may be remapped per project to an adapter set — see `apps/web/src/icons/README.md`). Never import an icon library (Phosphor, Lucide, MUI icons for decoration) directly in a page.
- Every icon component implements `NextureIconsProps` (`size`, `variant`, `className`, `oneTone`) and is a default export. The props type and the size helpers live in `src/icons/nexture-icons.ts`, which imports NO icon (every icon file imports it).
- `src/icons/icon-registry.tsx` (`IconMap`, `NextureIcons`) maps names to components and imports the whole set. Use it only where the icon name is data (the dashboard menu, a catalog icon typed by the operator); a client component that imports it ships every icon to the browser.
- Alternative sets live in sibling folders (`src/icons/phosphor/`, ...) with identical file names; gaps are filled by `npm run icons:stubs -w @flyee/web` (fallback re-exports, never overwritten).
- Adapters import icon libs from their SSR-safe entry (e.g. `@phosphor-icons/react/dist/ssr`) so they work in Server Components.

===== .claude/rules/marketing.md =====

# Marketing layer boundaries

> The `marketing-page` skill and `docs/DESIGN.md` were written for flyee.club: their examples (the app store, the terminal, the founders offer, an English twin of every page) do not apply to ONE, while their rules do. How the site came to be is in `apps/web/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

- **One design system.** Every public page composes the primitives in `apps/web/src/components/marketing/`: `Section`/`Container`/`SectionHeader` plus the archetypes listed in `catalog.json`. Never hand-tuned per-page spacing or widths, never a parallel stylesheet vocabulary.
- The `marketing-page` skill is MANDATORY for any create/edit/add-section under `app/[locale]/(marketing)`, `app/[locale]/(funil)` or `components/marketing`. The `PreToolUse` hook (`.claude/hooks/marketing-guard.mjs`) loads it automatically on Write/Edit in all three, and the `PostToolUse` lint (`.claude/hooks/marketing-lint.mjs`) checks every written file there. A file changed by a script bypasses both hooks: load the skill yourself and run the lint on it by hand.
- **Visual direction.** ONE has not committed its own direction yet: the palette (`theme-blue`), the logo and the type are provisional. Until it does, new pages and sections INHERIT what the components already do. Never restyle the UI or change the palette, the type or the logo unless the user explicitly asks. Adding a section triggers a whole-page coherence pass so all sections stay aesthetically aligned.
- **One language, in the path.** ONE is written in Portuguese only. Every public page lives under `app/[locale]/` in a folder named after its address, and is declared in `apps/web/src/i18n/routing.ts` (`pathnames`). That declaration is also what makes the middleware treat it as public: there is no separate list of public pages. Sign-in, the logged area, checkout and the admin have no locale in the URL.
- Internal links on public surfaces go through `LocaleLink` (`components/marketing/locale-link.tsx`, also as MUI's `LinkComponent`) or `localizeHref`: `href` is the internal path and the link renders the public address. Links to `/auth/*` and other non-public routes pass through unchanged.
- An INDEXED page also goes to `apps/web/src/app/sitemap.ts`. A `noindex` page (`/espera/confirmar`, `/descadastro`, any campaign page) stays out of the sitemap and is named in its exclusion comment. Indexing is decided by `metadata` + `sitemap.ts`, never by the route group.
- `/ajuda` and `/blog` are DB-managed: content is written in `/admin/help` / `/admin/blog` and fetched through `apps/web/src/lib/public-content.ts` (anon client, published rows). Content that could not be read is never shown as an empty list. Markdown renders via `components/marketing/markdown-prose.tsx`. Never interpolate DB content as raw HTML.
- SEO is part of every page: exactly one `<h1>` (the page title: `SectionHeader as="h1"` / `PricingSection headingAs="h1"` when the lead is not a `<Hero>`), a title + description via `generateMetadata` that spreads `publicPageMetadata({ path, locale })` from `lib/seo.ts` (canonical, Open Graph URL and locale), and structured data through `<JsonLd>` (`components/marketing/json-ld.tsx`), never a hand-written `<script>`. `Organization`/`FAQPage`/`Product` schemas are already emitted by the layout/`Faq`/`PricingSection`; do not duplicate them. Inner pages add `BreadcrumbJsonLd`. A missing page answers a real 404 and a moved one a real redirect: never put a loading boundary (`loading.tsx`, or a `<Suspense>` around the children of a layout) above a public page, because the response would start before `notFound()` or `redirect()` runs and go out as a 200.
- Marketing copy lives in the `marketing` namespace of `packages/content/messages/pt-BR.json`. No hardcoded strings.
- **Blocking on every public page**: exactly one `<h1>`, real `alt` text, no fabricated testimonials, metrics, logos or case results, prices and limits read from data (`plans`), no struck-through price and no "from/to" pair. Every number on a public page comes from the database.
- **What the site may say about the product.** ONE is software for law firms, sold by a technology company: it never promises the outcome of a lawsuit, an amount of compensation or a time to judgment, never speaks to passengers as if it were a law firm, and never says a step is automatic when a lawyer decides it (filing is assisted: the lawyer reviews and files with their own login).
- **What the site sells: ONE's core** (the owner, 2026-10-27). The copy is about the AI automation of a mass-litigation firm's cases: the client served on the firm's WhatsApp, the papers checked, the piece written, the deadlines counted, the filing package built, the firm choosing what a person reviews. It is never about an application built on it, such as the flight monitor that writes to passengers (Direito do Passageiro in `docs/PRODUCT.md`, the owner's "viagem segura"): a module is named at most in a line, as the first one, never in a title, the hero or the drawn screens.
- **Copy rules**: Portuguese, plain; no dash (— or –), no exclamation mark and no emoji in any visible text, `alt` and `aria-label` included (© and → stay, on purpose), and none of the banned words: desbloqueie, potencialize, sem esforço, soluções inovadoras. Where a dash would go, write a colon, a comma or a new sentence; separate items with "·"; a missing value hides its line instead of printing a placeholder.
